comparisons.peer_summary: The company offers flexible and inclusive benefits, including global parental and bereavement leave and financial assistance for adoption or surrogacy, while embracing hybrid and remote work options alongside in-person collaboration.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD disclose a hybrid work model that balances remote options with in-person collaboration to support talent strategy. Intel specifies a 'hybrid-first' approach with no company-wide mandate on on-site days, focusing on output. AMD similarly embraces 'hybrid and remote work as options' while noting the value of in-person collaboration. AMD's disclosure is broader, including specific mention of inclusive benefits like parental leave and adoption assistance, whereas Intel focuses on the operational flexibility and recruitment breadth of the hybrid model.

sentences.text: Our "hybrid-first" approach to working was informed by employees surveyed around the globe and involves the majority of our employees splitting their time between working remotely and in the office.
Currently, there is no company-wide mandate on the number of days per week employees should be on site or how they should collaborate.

We focus on flexibility and choice in our benefits that resonate with a multi-generational workforce as well as offering inclusive benefits that support our DB&I objectives, such as global parental and bereavement leave, and financial assistance to build a family through adoption or surrogacy.
While we believe that there is unique collaboration that can occur when employees meet in person, we embrace flexibility with hybrid and remote work as options for our employees.

comparisons.peer_summary: NVIDIA supports a flexible work environment, including the ability to work from home under certain conditions, to support diverse hiring, retention, and employee engagement. During fiscal year 2025, the company will maintain this flexibility along with a company-wide policy of two days off per quarter for rest and recharge.
comparisons.comparison: Intel and NVIDIA both describe a flexible work environment that allows employees to work from home to support recruitment and retention. Intel's policy is 'hybrid-first' with no mandate on on-site days, while NVIDIA supports the 'ability to work from home under certain conditions.' Both companies explicitly link this flexibility to hiring and retention benefits. NVIDIA adds a distinct policy element not present in Intel's FY2024 disclosure: a company-wide provision of two days off per quarter for rest and recharge.

This flexibility supports diverse hiring, retention, and employee engagement, which we believe makes NVIDIA a great place to work.
